transcript:
This is NPR News Now.
The latest headlines every hour.
Live from NPR News in Washington, I'm Louise Schiavone.
President Trump made history this week with the first-ever trilateral meeting with the
leaders of China and Russia.
The question is, will there be an immediate or lasting impact?
NPR's Ron Elving has more.
It could have if these various vows of peaceful cooperation bear fruit, or if these vaunted
trade deals come to pass, but what we do know at this point is that Russia this week launched
one of its most massive assaults against Ukraine since it first invaded that country in 2022.
Assaults against civilian targets that also struck Poland, the NATO alloy of the U.S.
And it makes a difference that Trump was more interested in meeting with Chinese President
Xi than he was in confronting that country's efforts to obtain the most advanced American
computer chips.
NPR's Ron Elving, the U.N. says there have been more Israeli settler attacks on the Palestinian
olive harvest this year than in any other year since record keeping began.
And NPR's Lauren Freyer has details.
The United Nations cites more than 400 Israeli settler attacks since September on Palestinian
olive farmers, as well as activists, journalists, and diplomats who try to help them.
And it says more than 55,000 pounds of produce have been vandalized or stolen.
This weekend, a Palestinian lawmaker in Israel's parliament shared video he says shows Israeli
settlers stealing fruit and vegetables from Palestinian vendors in the occupied West Bank,
accusing settlers who serve in Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's far-right government
of allowing them to do so.
The Israeli military has said it seeks to prevent friction during the olive harvest,
but the U.N. accuses it of, quote, "acquiescent support and participation in attacks."
Lauren Freyer, NPR News, Tel Aviv.
"Ice agents will be allowed to keep wearing face coverings while making arrests in Connecticut."
A federal judge ruled the state's attempt to ban mask wearing was unconstitutional.
From member station WSHU, Molly Ingram reports.
Earlier this year, the state legislature passed a law that in part banned ice agents from
wearing masks to hide their identity and required them to wear name badges.
It was challenged by the Trump administration shortly after.
In a preliminary injunction on Friday, a Biden-appointed federal judge in New Haven ruled the law
violated the supremacy clause of the U.S. Constitution.
Similar decisions have been made by judges in New York, California and Pennsylvania.
In Connecticut, community members and officials have long complained the law had no teeth.
Even Governor Ned Lamont said the state would not arrest agents for refusing to wear masks.
For NPR News, I'm Molly Ingram in Fairfield.
One of the FBI's 10 most wanted fugitives has been captured by Mexican authorities.
Mexico's defense cabinet says seven alleged cartel gunmen, four Mexican soldiers were
killed in a fierce firefight that erupted in Sinaloa as Fosto Isidro Meza Flores was
apprehended.
This is NPR News.
President Trump is saying that he's prepared to work with the new Democratic-controlled
Congress to cap credit card interest rates.
Trump had talked about this on the 2024 campaign trail.
But the banking industry and a GOP majority were not interested.
Democrats and Trump have both back capping rates at 10 percent.
Funeral services for labor activist Dolores Huerta have ended in her final hometown Bakersfield,
California.
Amare Alvarez from member station KVPR has that story.
Members of Huerta's family and state leaders spoke about her legacy at her final goodbye.
America's Democratic governor-elect, Javier Becerra, highlighted her fight for farmworker
rights.
There's never been a day in my life without Dolores Huerta.
There was never a fight that I saw that didn't include Dolores Huerta.
Former President Bill Clinton and actress Jane Fonda appeared in video messages.
This event kept off a week of services that started with Huerta laying in honor in the
state capitol.
By the end of the night, everyone was on their feet, dancing to the Mexican-American group
Los Lobos.
For NPR, I'm Amare Alvarez in Bakersfield.
Katherine, Princess of Wales, appears in a new documentary about life after her cancer
diagnosis in 2024.
Entitled Healed, the project follows her as she attempts the Three Peaks Challenge, climbing
the highest mountains in Scotland, England, and Wales within 24 hours.
She completed the feat to raise money for the cancer charity of the Royal Marston Hospital
that treated her.
I'm Louise Quivone, NPR News.

topics.text: Trump holds first-ever trilateral meeting with Chinese and Russian leaders; impact uncertain
Russia launches one of its most massive assaults on Ukraine since 2022, striking Poland too
UN reports record Israeli settler attacks on Palestinian olive harvest, including produce theft in the West Bank
Federal judge in New Haven blocks Connecticut law banning ICE agents from wearing masks
Mexican authorities capture FBI top-10 fugitive Fausto Isidro Meza Flores in Sinaloa firefight
Trump says he will work with Democratic Congress to cap credit card interest rates at 10 percent
Funeral services for labor activist Dolores Huerta conclude in Bakersfield, California
Princess Catherine appears in documentary about life after cancer diagnosis, including Three Peaks Challenge
